title: Zanzibar: Google’s Consistent, Global Authorization System
algorithm_class: Consistency-aware distributed ReBAC authorization with version (zookie) tokens
supported_guarantee: Bounded staleness of permission evaluations via zookies/consistency tokens and monotonic per-user snapshot reads; global tuple-change ordering; planetary-scale operation verified in production at Google.
limitations_vs_candidate: Guarantees cover permission evaluation at the record-read boundary only: zookies do not label, track, or invalidate derived model-context artifacts (prompt segments, cached summaries, embedding pointers, retry payloads, fallback transports) after consent revocation, and no purpose/consent-epoch labels exist on cache lines.
mechanism_analysis: C1 reference and design source for POPETS arm B3: revocation propagates by tuple writes plus external-consistency reads, so a fresh-zookie check fails against stale permission state. The staleness key is the permission tuple, not the lineage of derived dispatch content; a cache entry derived before revocation is invisible to zookie validation at dispatch time, so the mechanism alone cannot enforce future dispatch noninterference. No official reference implementation exists (design paper); execution goes through the OpenFGA comparator instead.

title: OpenFGA: Zanzibar-inspired fine-grained authorization
algorithm_class: Zanzibar-inspired relationship-based authorization (ReBAC) with consistency tokens
supported_guarantee: Executable relationship-based checks with consistency tokens (minimize_latency=false) and fresh evaluation modes; pinned at tag v1.22.1 as registry baseline zanzibar-openfga (upstream revision 44054f542f64e9b9589dd26a595081b3d2cfd942, Apache-2.0, ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM, verified 2026-11-15).
limitations_vs_candidate: Consistency applies to relationship-tuple evaluation; no built-in representation of derived-artifact lineage, no reverse-edge invalidation of cached model contexts, and consent lifecycle must be encoded externally in the authorization model (ledger: policy/consent model mapping limits).
mechanism_analysis: Executable POPETS arm B3 path: the registry zanzibar-openfga entry is pinned to run the actual OpenFGA server binary at the pinned tag with synthetic fixtures only (not yet executed in this worktree; evaluation/venue2027 does not exist yet). The adapter must genuinely demonstrate derived-cache tagging support before comparative claims; otherwise B3 is reported NOT_RUN_EXTERNAL and is never replaced by a custom toy under the same name (execution contract rule 8). If lineage(d) cannot be represented, the C1/C3 falsification surface stays open.

title: Cedar policy language and authorization reference implementation
algorithm_class: ABAC/PBAC policy-as-code evaluation engine with schema validation
supported_guarantee: Executable fine-grained policy evaluation with type-checked schema and documented expressivity limits; pinned at tag v4.14.1 in the shared registry (cedar-opa-policy-decision-nonce-registry, upstream revision 47d82a8293354f235d3f8d092c71071706401741, Apache-2.0, ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM, verified 2026-11-15).
limitations_vs_candidate: Request-time policy decisions only: purpose can be encoded as an attribute, but there is no consent-epoch cache keying, no derived-artifact labeling, and no dependency-closure invalidation across prompt/summary/embedding/retry paths. Registry venues are ifip_sec/sacmat; for POPETS it is a citation-level comparator, not an arm.
mechanism_analysis: C1/C3 comparator: a Cedar decision can deny a dispatch at evaluation time, but the engine has no cache-invalidation primitive, so derived artifacts created under a previously-authorized policy epoch remain reusable without re-entering the decision point. Documents the policy-engine feature coverage (ledger relation: executable ABAC/PBAC comparator) the candidate's origin/purpose-labeled closure must exceed.

title: Open Policy Agent (OPA): policy-as-code engine
supported_guarantee: Executable per-request policy decisions over arbitrary structured inputs; recorded as the alternative PDP in registry entry cedar-opa-policy-decision-nonce-registry (OPA v1.22.4, commit ba39415db4b3c90cd68942a74b3cc2223ec2b23c, Apache-2.0, ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM, verified 2026-11-15).
limitations_vs_candidate: Stateless per-request evaluation: no built-in temporal consent, no derived-artifact lineage closure, no cache-invalidation primitive; purpose binding must be re-encoded by the caller at every dispatch (ledger relation: no built-in temporal consent unless encoded).
mechanism_analysis: C3 comparator: a per-dispatch OPA query over live-purpose clauses is the policy-layer analogue of the B2 always-recompute reference; it never touches derived state, so cached pre-revocation artifacts can be re-dispatched without a fresh decision. Used to verify that the rule-engine class does not already perform transitive, purpose-labeled invalidation of derived model-context artifacts.

title: Macaroons: Cookies with Contextual Caveats for Decentralized Authorization in the Cloud
algorithm_class: HMAC caveat-chain context-bound capability credentials (first-class attenuation)
supported_guarantee: Unrestricted root identifier attenuated by appended contextual caveats (actor, purpose, task, expiry, nonce) verified by an HMAC chain; delegation without key sharing; third-party caveats supported.
limitations_vs_candidate: Caveat satisfaction is evaluated at credential-verification time; artifacts derived while a caveat set was satisfied carry no binding into later cache lines, so cached derivations outlive caveat checks at dispatch time. Revocation requires re-issuance or short expiry, not lineage invalidation. No official reference implementation exists; third-party pymacaroons v0.13.0 (MIT) is registered only as an independent cross-check, not as the comparator.
mechanism_analysis: C5 reference (registry ifip_sec entry macaroon-hmac-caveats, FAITHFUL_PORT target with the official NDSS 2014 PDF SHA256 pinned): attenuation is a per-credential property, but a model-context cache entry is not a credential, so nothing in the construction re-checks caveats when a cached derivation is re-dispatched. Verifying this gap is the C5 falsification test; a verified caveat-bound extension covering derived-artifact re-dispatch at equal lineage density would falsify C5.

title: MUSE: Machine Unlearning Six-Way Evaluation for Language Models
algorithm_class: Machine unlearning evaluation taxonomy (six-way: knowledge, privacy, utility)
supported_guarantee: Defines six evaluation dimensions separating knowledge-extraction ability, privacy (membership-inference) regret, and utility regeneration for unlearning in language models.
limitations_vs_candidate: Threat model is influence removal from trained weights; it neither gates nor measures future dispatches of cached derived context after consent revocation and makes no dispatch-time noninterference claim. No redistributable upstream code pin exists (registry: taxonomy-only comparator, UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN).
mechanism_analysis: C2 boundary (registry muse-unlearning-comparator, POPETS arm): used conceptually to keep unlearning (weight influence) distinct from this paper's consent-lifecycle gating of downstream dispatches; no MUSE code is executed in the POPETS pipeline. Collapses C1+C2 only if a ledger-verified work defines consent-revocation-time, dispatch-time noninterference for cached model contexts.

title: FHIR R5 Consent, AuditEvent, Provenance resources
algorithm_class: Interoperability standard for consent, audit, and provenance structures
supported_guarantee: Structured Consent resources including purposeOfUse scope binding permitted data use to declared purposes; AuditEvent/Provenance structures record disclosures.
limitations_vs_candidate: Defines structures, not enforcement: no cache-invalidation semantics, no derived-artifact lineage, no dispatch-time gate, and no cost model for consent-triggered purges (ledger relation: structure/interoperability only).
mechanism_analysis: C1/C4 background: purposeOfUse supplies the vocabulary for forbidden_label(g,p) and motivates origin- and purpose-labeled keying of derived artifacts (the blueprint's purpose-bound cache keying reference); AuditEvent shapes the disclosure observation model. FHIR compliance alone is not clinical safety and does not pre-empt C4's consent-triggered purge cost analysis.

title: Guide to Attribute Based Access Control (ABAC) Definition and Considerations
algorithm_class: Normative ABAC vocabulary and design guidance (standard)
supported_guarantee: Formal attribute-based access-control vocabulary (subject/resource/action/environment attributes, including purpose) and policy-composition guidance (NIST SP 800-162, updated 2019).
limitations_vs_candidate: Vocabulary only: no cache model, no invalidation algorithm, no measurement of false-invalidation or availability costs, so no conformance or performance claim can be derived from it (ledger relation: formal authorization vocabulary and policy attributes).
mechanism_analysis: C4 background: supplies the attribute terms (purpose, consent epoch) used to state the candidate's keying labels in the SACMAT-portable oracle encodings; establishes that the standard defines no consent-triggered cache purge cost model, so C4 is not pre-empted by prior standardization.

title: TTL-only cache (blueprint arm B0; registry baseline ttl-only-cache)
algorithm_class: Time-to-live cache expiry, weak lower-bound control
supported_guarantee: Bounded cache-entry lifetime independent of consent events: entries expire after TTL regardless of policy state.
limitations_vs_candidate: No revocation listener: between revocation time t_r and TTL expiry every dispatch may re-send revoked context, so it is a weak lower bound expected to exhibit the leak class; it is not a strong competitor and must never be presented as one (registry notes: in-project; no upstream pin to verify).
mechanism_analysis: RQ1 lower bound: exhibits the unmitigated post-revocation window mechanism (expiry-only, no dependency labels). Parity fixture and exec_command are registered (evaluation/venue2027/popets/fixtures/ttl_only_cache_parity.json) but the implementation does not exist in the repository yet, hence UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN. A negative result with zero leakage witnesses anywhere including B0 falsifies RQ1 and with it C1.

title: Coarse cache purge on consent change (blueprint arm B1; registry baseline coarse-cache-purge-on-revocation)
algorithm_class: Full cache refresh on revocation (coarse invalidation), strong simple safety baseline
supported_guarantee: On any revocation event, purge all cached entries derived from the subject's context regardless of lineage: revocation-complete by over-invalidation.
limitations_vs_candidate: Pays availability/latency/false-invalidation costs growing with lineage density; no dependency labels, so authorized context for other grants and purposes is destroyed too; the candidate's origin- and purpose-labeled closure claims a measurable advantage against exactly this cost (C4).
mechanism_analysis: RQ3 competitor and strongest simple safety baseline: bounds the availability cost of the safety-first alternative. If B1's costs are already negligible across the factorial lineage-density grid (overlapping subject-clustered CIs on conditional cache hit and p95 latency, no interaction effect), the trade-off claim dies and novelty narrows to an engineering trade-off per the blueprint falsification rule.

title: Always-recompute authorized projection per dispatch (blueprint arm B2; registry baseline always-recompute-authorized-projection)
algorithm_class: Per-dispatch full recompute of the authorized projection, zero caching
supported_guarantee: Zero cached-derivation leakage by construction: every dispatch recomputes the authorized view from live source snapshots under live-purpose permission clauses.
limitations_vs_candidate: Maximum recomputation cost at every dispatch (no cache hits, no reuse); it is the privacy reference upper bound rather than an availability competitor and cannot exhibit cache-related false invalidation because it never caches.
mechanism_analysis: RQ1/RQ2 reference and C8 competing explanation: if B2 matches the candidate B4 with negligible overhead and zero leakage on the frozen confirmatory holdout, novelty narrows to an engineering performance trade-off and the GO decision flips at POPETS-rq_registry time (novelty contract conditionality). Disclosure-trace equivalence to B2 is the RQ2 TOST target; McNemar pairs B4 against B2 per subject history.

title: Zanzibar-like consistency-token authorization with derived-cache tagging (blueprint arm B3; registry baseline zanzibar-like-consistency-token-cache)
algorithm_class: Consistency-token authorization plus derived-cache tagging (Zanzibar design)
supported_guarantee: Adapter target: zookies/consistency tokens plus derived-tuple tagging per Zanzibar ATC 2019 Sec. 2.3-2.4 (registry target fidelity FAITHFUL_PORT with the paper SHA256 c57af6886593e778916b7ca60dcf049d90f75aee3eb07cf7e78f8565f93e0b0a pinned as revision).
limitations_vs_candidate: The in-project adapter does not exist yet; if it cannot genuinely represent derived-artifact lineage, B3 must be reported NOT_RUN_EXTERNAL and never replaced by a custom toy under the same name (execution contract rule 8). Paper-level guarantees cover permission staleness, not dispatch-content lineage.
mechanism_analysis: Strongest architecture baseline for RQ2: combines per-dispatch consistency-checked authorization with tagging of derived cache entries, making it the closest prior mechanism to the candidate. The executable path prefers the zanzibar-openfga ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM entry (OpenFGA v1.22.1) when semantics allow. Paired false-invalidation counts and disclosure equivalence against B3 feed the RQ2 sign-test/Wilcoxon comparison.

title: Purpose-bound cache keying (blueprint design reference: origin/purpose-labeled keys without reverse-edge closure)
venue: CLARA 2027 POPETS blueprint (in-design mechanism reference, not published prior work)
algorithm_class: Consent-epoch and purpose labels embedded in cache keys
supported_guarantee: Cache lines keyed by (subject, grant, purpose, policy/consent epoch): a consent change or revocation rotates the key space, forcing recompute for affected purposes on the next dispatch.
limitations_vs_candidate: Key rotation invalidates only entries whose key components change; derived artifacts reachable through transitive lineage (retry payloads, fallback transports, embedding pointers) whose keys stay stable are not invalidated - no reverse dependency edges, hence not revocation-complete. Not a published system, so it cannot by itself validate novelty.
mechanism_analysis: Mechanism-isolation reference derived from the blueprint method ('label derived artifacts at creation; reauthorize at every dispatch') with lineage closure removed: it isolates how much protection comes from keying alone versus dependency closure, the C3/RQ2 ablation surface. Recorded honestly as a design reference, not prior literature, so the novelty claim rests on the closure mechanism, not the keying; grounded in the novelty contract's origin- and purpose-labeled invalidation wording.
